title: The Salafi approach
hookLine: a movement to follow the early generations closely and avoid later additions, itself diverse

cards: A chain of people, hand to hand. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says something. A companion hears it and passes it on.
Someone who learned from that companion passes it on again. Al-Bukhari keeps a saying about those first links.
In paraphrase: the best people are my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them.

Some Muslims draw a plain conclusion: if the first links were the best, the surest way to practice Islam is to stand as close to them as you can. That's where today's movement starts, in its own words.

teach.b: First, the name, as Salafis explain it. They take it from a phrase, al-salaf al-salih, which they render as the righteous predecessors: the companions and the generations who learned from them.
A Salafi, in their own description, follows the Qur'an and the Sunnah as those early generations understood them. Second, what they avoid. Salafi teachers point to a hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim.

teach.h: IS IT SOMETHING NEW? THEN IT'S REJECTED.
teach.b: In paraphrase: whoever brings into this matter of ours something that is not part of it, it is rejected.
So they are wary of practices they see as later additions, and ask of any devotion: did the Prophet and his companions do this? Tawhid, Allah's oneness, sits at the center of how they teach.
Third, the movement is itself diverse. There is no single Salafi headquarters. Some teachers focus on study and personal practice and stay out of public life; others take part in it.
Salafis argue with each other about method, about politics, about how strict to be with someone who disagrees. Lumping them together misses those arguments. Fourth, the conversation around them.
Muslims who are not Salafi also love the first generations, and say so.
Scholars of the traditional schools hold that the schools and the long line of later scholarship are how a Muslim reaches those generations faithfully, not a step away from them.
Salafis answer that the texts should be read directly, with the early generations as the guide.
Each side says it is following the companions. They differ about the road back.

how: Salafi Muslims describe their approach as following the Qur'an and the Sunnah as the companions and the generations after them understood them, studying the texts directly and avoiding devotions they regard as later additions; they differ among themselves on method and on public life.

o: following Islam as the first generations did
a Sufi path of chanting and remembrance
a political party founded in modern times

games.q: the Salafi approach — tap the pairs.

s: Salafis all agree with each other on method and politics
they argue among themselves; some stay out of public life, others take part.
Salafis take their name from the early generations they aim to follow
they explain it from al-salaf al-salih, the righteous predecessors.
only Salafis honor the first generations
Muslims of the traditional schools love them too, and say the schools are their road back to them.

games.q: you're a Salafi teacher and someone asks about a devotion you've never heard of. what's the first question you ask?
o: is it popular where you live?
did the Prophet and his companions do this?
does it feel meaningful to you?
games.why: in their own description, Salafis measure a practice by whether the first generations did it, pointing to the hadith that something new brought into the religion is rejected.

practice: Let each breath be one link in the chain from the hook: the Prophet, a companion, the one who learned from that companion.
Stay with the chain for a few breaths without judging anyone in it, letting a movement describe itself before anyone else describes it. If you pray, make your own prayer in your own words.

wordCard.voice: The Salafi approach. A movement that aims to follow the Qur'an and the Sunnah as the first generations understood them, wary of later additions, and diverse inside itself. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: one who follows the salaf, the predecessors, as Salafis explain their own name.

carryVoice: Your line: back to the first generations. Each side walks toward the companions by its own road. That's today, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2652 (the best people are my generation, then those after them, then those after them)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2697; Sahih Muslim 1718 (whoever introduces into this matter of ours what is not of it, it is rejected)
